To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the combined DNA extraction and elution technique is operationally attractive for high throughput assessment and that PCR sensitivity is influenced by the choice of target gene, the amount and source (whole blood or plasma) of filter paper material used for DNA extraction.

combined DNA extraction and antigen elution from filter paper is a useful approach to quantify malaria transmission intensity in low-endemicity areas, and that the choice of target gene can have an important impact on PCR sensitivity for the detection of malaria infection.

combined DNA extraction and elution of antibodies from filter paper blood spots is an attractive approach for high-throughput assessment of cumulative malaria transmission and current infection prevalence.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development and evaluation of a combined DNA extraction and elution method for the assessment of transmission intensity in epidemiologic studies.
the development of a new method to measure the intensity of malaria transmission and to improve its operational practicability.
a methodological approach for the assessment of cumulative malaria transmission intensity and current infection status in epidemiological studies using filter paper blood spots.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the combined DNA and antibody extraction method provides an attractive and operationally feasible approach for high throughput seroepidemiology and molecular epidemiology in malaria endemic settings.

the choice of PCR target gene and the source of filter paper for DNA extraction are important for PCR sensitivity, but that the use of a combined DNA extraction and elution method for antibody detection does not affect the outcome.
the combined DNA extraction and elution technique is a valid method to measure antibody levels in epidemiological studies, but PCR assays should be optimized for each specific situation.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
combined antibody/DNA extractions are an operationally attractive and reliable approach to measure malaria exposure and infection prevalence in epidemiological studies.

the use of combined DNA extraction and antigen/antibody elution from filter paper blood spots for the assessment of cumulative malaria transmission and current malaria infection prevalence is feasible and can be used to inform the design and implementation of malaria control programmes.
combined extraction and eluting is a useful approach for antibody and DNA detection in epidemiological surveys.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the choice of DNA extraction method should be informed by the intended downstream application.
the use of filter paper blood spots as a source of DNA and antibodies is a valuable and practical tool for the assessment of cumulative exposure and recent infection in malaria endemic settings.
a single filter paper blood spot can provide both DNA and antibody material to quantify malaria exposure and infection in epidemiological studies, thereby enhancing operational practicability.
